items.title: A symplectic Hilbert hotel
items.summary: We construct a smooth global symplectomorphism of an infinite dimensional separable Hilbert space mapping a ball of large radius to a subset of a cylinder of small radius. This symplectomorphism and its inverse map bounded sets to bounded sets. This example shows that Gromov's non-squeezing theorem does not generalize to infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces without further assumptions.

items.title: A $(17/7-o(1))n$ Circuit Lower Bound for Binary-Encoded 3-SAT
items.summary: We strengthen the elementary $n-1$ circuit lower bound for a specified binary encoding of 3-SAT to $(17/7)n-O(n\log\log n/\log n)$ gates over the full two-input Boolean basis, with unrestricted depth and sharing. For each integer $w\ge5$, we encode 3-CNF formulas with exactly $m=2^w-1$ clauses over $m$ available variables using $n=3m(w+1)$ bits. The proof embeds Boolean tests in variable identifiers while retaining $n-o(n)$ free bits, and combines weighted gate elimination with a nonlinear-gate lower bound from the tests' full algebraic degree over $\mathbb F_2$. We provide Lean proofs of the finite inequality and the asymptotic bound for arbitrary acyclic binary circuits.

items.title: Odd Chromatic Number of Graph Classes: Bounds and Structural Results
items.summary: A proper coloring of a graph $G$ is called an \emph{odd coloring} if, for every non-isolated vertex $v\in V(G)$, there exists a color that occurs an odd number of times in the open neighborhood of $v$. For a graph $G$, the minimum number of colors required for such a coloring is called the {\em odd chromatic number}, denoted by $\chi_{o}(G)$. The odd chromatic number has been well-studied from both combinatorial and algorithmic perspectives, and several bounds on $\chi_o(G)$ are known. In this paper, we establish tight bounds on $\chi_o(G)$ for several graph classes. In particular, we obtain the following results: 1. items.title: Fermat costs and path-dependent first-passage percolation
items.summary: We introduce a path-dependent and space-inhomogeneous first-passage percolation (FPP) model in the continuum. Inspired by Euclidean FPP, it is defined through a sample of points drawn from a common density function on a Riemannian manifold. In Euclidean FPP, the cost of each step in a discrete path is given by its length raised to the power $\alpha>1$. In our model, the power $\alpha$ increases as the path progresses, governed by a control mechanism. Consequently, the resulting percolation cost is not a distance. However, we prove a shape theorem showing that, as the number of points goes to infinity, the percolation costs converge to deterministic space-time integrals along curves in the…

items.title: Effect of dark matter and scalar-cut potential on the macroscopic properties of neutron stars: A chiral quark mean field approach
items.summary: We investigate the effects of fermionic dark matter (DM) and scalar-cut potential ($U_{\text{cut}}(\phi)$) on the equation of state (EOS) and macroscopic properties of neutron stars. The baryonic matter consists of neutrons, protons, electrons, and muons under the $\beta$-equilibrium and is described within the chiral SU(3) quark mean-field (CQMF) model. In this framework, quarks are confined within baryons, whose properties are modified through the exchange of scalar fields $\sigma$, $\zeta$, and $\delta$, and vector fields $\omega$ and $\rho$. The DM is modelled as a self-interacting fermionic fluid with scalar $\varphi_D$ and vector $V_D^\mu$ mediators. The baryonic and DM fluids…

items.title: Geometric distinguishability of two-source gravitational-wave signals from the extrinsic geometry of the single-source waveform manifold
items.summary: Overlapping gravitational-wave signals can produce strong degeneracies in which a multi-source waveform is accurately represented by a single effective source. We formulate this source-confusion problem geometrically by treating the family of single-source waveforms as an embedded manifold in the noise-weighted detector Hilbert space. We introduce the distance-to-manifold statistic, defined as the minimum residual obtained by fitting a waveform with the single-source model, and show that its squared value is directly related to the maximized likelihood difference between two-source and single-source hypotheses in the noiseless limit. For two sources with nearby parameters, perturbative…

items.title: Equivariant Localization for $K(n)$-Local Gromov-Witten Invariants with Applications to Gopakumar-Vafa Invariants
items.summary: For certain complex-oriented $K(n)$-local cohomology theories, we establish equivariant localization formulas for global Kuranishi charts and a Riemann-Roch formula. We apply these formulas to compute the genus-zero Gromov-Witten invariants of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)$ at odd primes, obtaining a residue formula in terms of the formal group law of the chosen complex orientation. As an application, we derive a multiple-cover formula expressing the genus-zero Morava $K$-theoretic Gromov-Witten invariants of closed symplectic Calabi-Yau threefolds in terms of their Gopakumar-Vafa invariants.

items.title: Flavor-resolved screening length of a moving quarkonium in a lattice-calibrated holographic QCD plasma
items.summary: We compute the screening length \(L_s\) of a moving heavy quark-antiquark pair in a lattice-calibrated Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton background for pure-glue, two-flavor, and \(2+1\)-flavor matter. Parallel and perpendicular orientations are considered at finite temperature, baryon chemical potential, and rapidity. \(L_s\) decreases monotonically with \(T\) and \(\eta\) in every flavor sector, and for the flavored systems also with \(\mu\). The perpendicular screening length is systematically smaller than the parallel one. At zero density and \(T=0.3\ \mathrm{GeV}\), the ordering \(L_s^{(N_f=0)}>L_s^{(N_f=2)}>L_s^{(N_f=2+1)}\) holds in this calibration, and a lattice check of the static flavor…

items.title: Vector boson scattering in composite Higgs models
items.summary: Vector boson scattering is a powerful tool to test the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking. We focus on Composite Higgs models with an underlying fermionic description and assume that only one pseudo Nambu-Goldstone boson contributes to electroweak symmetry breaking, which we identify as the Higgs state of the Standard Model. In these scenarios, LHC data imply lower bounds on the predicted resonances below 2 TeV depending on the scenario. Using $WZjj$ production as a benchmark, we demonstrate that the tails of various distributions nevertheless show significant deviations from Standard Model predictions. This holds in particular for the case of longitudinally polarised vector bosons.

items.title: Post-Newtonian expansion of the energy and angular momentum flux radiated to infinity: Eccentric-equatorial orbits about a Kerr black hole
items.summary: We present analytical expressions for the energy and angular momentum fluxes radiated to infinity by a (nonspinning) point mass in an eccentric-equatorial orbit about a Kerr black hole. These results build upon our previous work involving point masses on eccentric orbits about a Schwarzschild black hole. We now adopt the Teukolsky formalism in first-order black hole perturbation theory to extend our methods to Kerr. We obtain the expressions using the method of Mano, Suzuki, and Takasugi, which provides infinite-series analytical solutions to the Teukolsky equation that we generate using Mathematica. The expressions presented are obtained as a double expansion in the post-Newtonian (PN)…

items.title: Gray II, K\"ahler Nullity and Ricci Flow on Generalized Flag Manifolds with Two Isotropy Summands
items.summary: We investigate Gray's second curvature identity, K\"ahler nullity, and homogeneous Ricci flow on generalized flag manifolds with two isotropy summands. We prove that every invariant metric satisfies Gray's second identity for both invariant almost complex structures. For the non-integrable structure, the K\"ahler nullity is trivial except at a distinguished metric ratio, where it coincides with the vertical distribution of a homogeneous fibration. This distribution is integrable and has totally geodesic leaves. For the integrable structure, the K\"ahler nullity exhibits a different behavior and need not be integrable away from the K\"ahler locus. Finally, we reduce the normalized…

items.title: Eigendecomposition for instantons via infinity-category
items.summary: Suppose $L$ is a framed link in a balanced sutured manifold $(M, \gamma)$. We construct a link spectral sequence in sutured instanton homology. For properly embedded surfaces in $M$ disjoint from $L$, we refine the spectral sequence to preserve the induced multi-grading. We use $\infty$-categories to encode homotopical information from instanton theory. In particular, we obtain a simultaneous eigendecomposition of homotopy-coherently commutative operators on a chain complex or a hypercube complex. As the algebraic foundation for subsequent work of the second author and collaborators, we construct the mixed hypercube by combining the hypercubes of positive and negative bypass maps. This…

items.title: A Polynomial-Time Best-of-Both-Worlds Algorithm for Matroid Semi-Bandit Problems
items.summary: Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader (FTPL) offers a computationally attractive framework for online learning, with recent advances establishing Best-of-Both-Worlds (BOBW) guarantees for various bandit settings. For matroid semi-bandits, existing methods offering such guarantees primarily rely on Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL), which requires solving an optimization problem at each round. We establish BOBW guarantees for FTPL with Fr\'echet and Pareto distributions with a certain parameter with geometric resampling in the matroid semi-bandit problem, showing that FTPL can simultaneously achieve the minimax-optimal $O(\sqrt{mdT})$ regret in adversarial setting and a logarithmic regret in…

items.title: Optical appearance of a non-commutative black hole surrounded by an accretion disk
items.summary: We investigate the optical appearance of a non--commutative Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a transparent, geometrically thin emitting disk. A Lorentzian matter distribution supplies the effective exterior metric. We compute photon trajectories, disk transfer functions, and the observed bolometric intensity for static and circular emitters, taking into account gravitational redshift, orbital time dilation, and Doppler modulation. At fixed asymptotic mass, increasing $\theta=\Theta/M^2$ from zero to $0.03$ reduces the critical impact parameter by approximately $16.1\%$ and the innermost stable circular orbit radius by $23.7\%$. items.title: Hypergraph Ramsey Numbers via Oriented Palette Constructions
items.summary: Given a family $\mathcal F$ of $k$-graphs, the Ramsey number $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ is the minimum $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of $K_N^{(k)}$ yields either a red copy of some $F\in\mathcal F$ or a blue copy of $K_n^{(k)}$. In particular, if $\mathcal F=\{F\}$, we write $r_k(F,n)$. In this paper, we use oriented palette constructions and the hypergraph container method to obtain a lower bound on $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ for special families $\mathcal F$. More precisely, we independently label lower-dimensional faces and use the palette to exclude prescribed red configurations, while a container argument controls the size of blue cliques. As a first application of our theorem…

items.title: On the moduli space of nonpositively curved metrics on a product with a torus
items.summary: We prove that if $N$ is a closed smooth manifold admitting a Riemannian metric of negative sectional curvature and $T^k$ is the $k$-dimensional torus, then there is a retraction from the moduli space of nonpositively curved Riemannian metrics on $T^k\times N$ onto the moduli space of flat metrics on $T^k$. As an application, we combine our retraction with Tuschmann and Wiemeler's work on the rational topology of the moduli space of flat metrics on $T^k$ to deduce that the moduli space of nonpositively curved metrics on $T^k\times N$ has nontrivial higher rational homotopy and cohomology groups when $k\geq5$.

items.title: Hashing Theorems Modulo Rewrites and Binder Permutation Enables Equivalence Search over 200k Mathlib Theorems
items.summary: Like all code, Lean libraries accumulate technical debt and structural deficiencies over the course of their development. A particular concern is duplicate theorems: different parts of a big library can unwittingly contain and prove the same theorem, duplicating maintenance efforts. Tools can help detect redundancy and clean up. For instance, Mathlib's duplicate-declarations linter compares theorem types syntactically after sorting top-level binders and erasing binder information and universe levels. items.title: A decomposition of Hamiltonian matrices with symplectic kernels and its application to Williamson's diagonal form
items.summary: In this paper, we establish a decomposition of Hamiltonian matrices with symplectic kernels, which extends the main result in [K. D. items.title: A complete knot invariant from grid diagrams
items.summary: Using grid diagrams, we define an infinite graph associated to each knot type. We prove that the isomorphism class of this grid graph is a complete invariant of the knot, up to mirroring. items.title: Low-Rank Tensor Representations for Efficient Multimarginal Optimal Transport
items.summary: Multimarginal Optimal Transport (MOT) suffers from exponential computational and memory costs in the number of marginals, as transport plans are represented by high-dimensional tensors. This structure enables efficient algorithms with a low memory footprint. We establish approximation bounds for the resulting low-rank formulations and demonstrate experimentally that the proposed algorithms substantially reduce computational time while achieving solutions with low transport cost.

items.title: Hypergraph Structural Entropy-Enhanced Hierarchy-Aware Semi-Supervised Graph Classification
items.summary: Semi-supervised graph classification aims to learn graph-level representations by leveraging a large number of unlabeled graphs alongside a small set of labeled ones, effectively mitigating the issue of label scarcity. Despite significant progress by various semi-supervised learning strategies, complex relationships among graph vertices beyond pairwise edges, especially hierarchical structures, remain underexplored by existing methods. In this work, we propose a Hypergraph Structural Entropy-Enhanced hierarchy-aware framework, namely HypSEE, for semi-supervised graph classification. items.title: Compactness from fractional momentum bounds and weak solutions of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations
items.summary: We consider the barotropic Navier--Stokes equations on ${\mathbb R}^3$ with constant viscosities, finite mass and finite energy. For every $\gamma>1$, a local bound on the momentum $m=\rho u$ in $L^2_tH^{-1+\sigma}_x$, $\sigma>0$, gives strong local convergence of the densities under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1. For $\gamma>9/8$ we prove, uniformly along the approximations, $$ \|I_{1-\alpha}m\|_{L^2(I\times{\mathbb R}^3)}\leq C_{I,\alpha} \qquad\text{for some }\alpha>0,\quad I\Subset(0,\infty).$$ Here $I_s$ is the spatial Riesz potential. Together with tightness of the energy at spatial infinity, this gives a global finite-energy renormalized weak solution.

items.summary: Consider the motion of a rigid body moving into a viscous incompressible fluid that fills the whole space in 3D. We adopt a monolithic approach and carry out the spectral analysis to deduce the large time behavior of the fluid-structure semigroup, where the shape of the body is allowed to be arbitrary. items.title: Subsolar neutron star-black hole binaries from collapsars: Gravitational waveform models and detectability in current searches
items.summary: Detecting subsolar objects in binary mergers would be an exceptional discovery in gravitational wave astronomy. So far, dedicated searches for subsolar coalescences reported no confident detections, setting upper bounds on their merger rate. Given that standard stellar evolution is not able to produce subsolar candidates, a confident detection would point either to new physics or to unconventional astrophysical pathways. items.summary: We investigate higher-curvature corrections to black-hole thermodynamics in quasitopological gravity using perturbative Euclidean-action methods. Static, spherically symmetric black holes provide a benchmark for the action expansion, while our main application concerns five-dimensional, asymptotically flat, rotating black holes with equal angular momenta. For Einstein gravity supplemented by Gauss--Bonnet and cubic quasitopological interactions, we compute the Gibbs free energy through next-to-next-to-leading order, retaining both quadratic and cubic corrections. items.title: Melvin-type Electromagnetized Kerr Black Hole in Kaluza-Klein and Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion Theories
items.summary: A naive application of solution-generating techniques to construct Melvin-type rotating black holes in the Kaluza-Klein (KK) theory in the presence of both electric and magnetic external fields generically introduces an undesirable Taub-swirling twist term. We investigate its origin and modify the electromagnetization procedure, thereby constructing an exact solution of the Melvin-type electromagnetized Kerr black hole in the KK theory without the swirling term. We also obtain the analogous solution in the Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion (EMDA) theory. items.title: Comment on "Exact, nonsingular black holes from a phantom DBI field as primordial dark matter"
items.summary: We demonstrate that the metric and scalar configuration proposed in Ref.~[1] do not satisfy the complete set of field equations of the Dirac-Born-Infeld (DBI) field theory minimally coupled to general relativity on a radial domain containing the event horizon. The physical DBI branch for this gravitational setup terminates outside the event horizon. Thus, the proposed configuration does not describe a black hole solution of that theory.

items.title: Holography at finite resolution: zero-point length in AdS/CFT

As a boundary resolution scale, $l_0$ filters the source of a bulk scalar in anti-de Sitter space and yields an exactly solvable boundary response that is ultraviolet finite without a hard cutoff and inherits the power-law tails of the zero-point-length kernel. We show that this filter is the source-normalized bulk-to-boundary transfer function of a $\nu=1$ scalar evaluated at radial depth $z=l_0$. items.title: Quadratic Convexity for Closed and Free Boundary High Codimension Mean Curvature Flow
items.summary: We introduce quadratic convexity for mean curvature flow in high codimension. It combines quantitative convexity in the mean curvature direction with control of the full second fundamental form. Strict Andrews-Baker quadratic pinching implies quadratic convexity, while the new inequality also admits curvature tensors beyond the critical quadratic ratio. For compact connected closed submanifolds of dimension $n\geq5$, we prove preservation of quadratic convexity and convergence in finite time to a round point. items.title: Boundary preparation and anomalous relaxation near a black hole exceptional point
items.summary: We study the relaxation of a Robin scalar field near a stable exceptional point of a planar Schwarzschild AdS black hole, where finite boundary driving controls the recovery time without changing the leading decay rate at linear order. When the zeroth moment vanishes while the first remains nonzero, the linear time factor is eliminated, leaving an ordinary exponential decay. items.summary: For $\kappa\in(0,4]$, we prove a Cameron--Martin theorem for the welding law induced by SLE$_\kappa$ loop measure. Under simultaneous left and right composition $h\mapsto\varphi\circ h\circ\psi^{-1}$, the transformed law is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to the original law exactly when both maps belong to the Weil--Petersson group, and is mutually singular otherwise. items.title: Combinatorial Properties of The Giant Under Supercritical Percolation
items.summary: We study combinatorial properties, such as diameter and long paths and cycles, of the giant component of percolated graphs. items.title: On metric multiplicative Diophantine approximation
items.summary: Gallagher's theorem (1962) gives a Khintchine-type dichotomy for the Lebesgue measure of the set of multiplicatively $\psi$-approximable points in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \geq 2$, for monotonic functions $\psi$. We establish this dichotomy for arbitrary functions $\psi$, proving a conjecture of Beresnevich, Haynes, and Velani (2013).

items.title: ER=EPR and IMP wormholes in quantum gravity
items.summary: We analyze and refine the ER=EPR conjecture by studying IMP (Isenberg, Mazzeo and Pollack \cite{Isenberg:2001qe}) wormholes in QFT and quantum gravity, in the AdS/CFT context. IMP wormholes are solutions to the Einstein equations constructed from another general solution of Einstein's equations by gluing a handle on a Cauchy slice with a constant mean curvature, so that the initial data on the slice does not change in the regions away from the handle. This is made possible by using what is called the conformal method. items.title: Torsion order and the next-to-top term of knot Floer homology
items.summary: Sivek conjectured that, for every nontrivial knot $K\subset S^3$, the dimension of the next-to-top term of $\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(K)$ is at least that of the top term. We show that this inequality holds for knots with $U$-torsion order one in either the minus theory $\mathrm{HFK}^-$ or the unoriented theory $\mathrm{HFK}'$. Combined with Eftekhary's work, this implies that knots with rational unknotting number one satisfy the conjecture. In particular, the result applies to every nontrivial satellite knot whose pattern can be unknotted in the solid torus by a single rational tangle replacement.

items.title: Four consistent estimates of $H_0$ from a $\Lambda$CDM inference network given CMB data
items.summary: We organize inferences from cosmic microwave background (CMB) data, of the current rate of expansion, $H_0$, into a network whose structure is informed by a scaling symmetry of the Einstein-Boltzmann evolution equations. There are four distinct routes through this network from a calibrating anchor to $H_0$. Given key assumptions of the $\Lambda$CDM model, they are mutually consistent. This consistency is a significant feature of the $\Lambda$CDM model's compatibility with CMB data. The redundancy in $H_0$ determinations illuminates a hurdle to resolving the $H_0$ tension with alternative cosmological models.

For an arbitrary characteristic function $h(p)$, we derive a constrained first-order system in the static, asymptotically empty state. items.summary: We introduce a semigroup-based construction of Gaussian process (GP) priors. items.title: Measuring the Neutrino Mass with $^{241}$Pu
items.summary: Tritium has long been the isotope of choice for measurements of the absolute neutrino mass. Its low nuclear mass leads to substantial recoil energy, limiting measurements with both molecular tritium ($T_2$) and atomic tritium bound to a substrate. With a beta-decay endpoint energy and half-life similar to those of tritium, but a much larger nuclear mass, $^{241}$Pu may offer an interesting alternative. Its principal challenge is background from the beta decay of $^{237}$U. We discuss strategies for suppressing this background and compare the projected neutrino-mass sensitivities of $^{241}$Pu and tritium as a function of the background suppression.

items.title: Lean Census: A Distributional Analysis of AI-Generated Lean Code
items.summary: We compare two human-written and four AI-generated Lean libraries with Mathlib through the distributions of simple statistics of their code. For each library we measure inline claims in proofs, proof length, how often each declaration is used, and design choices such as instances and private declarations, and we read each against the variation among Mathlib's own areas. The AI-generated libraries have more inline claims per theorem, longer proofs, fewer instances, and more private declarations than the human-written ones. We release the code for the analysis as a package, lean-census, at https://github.com/project-numina/lean-census.

items.title: Finite-Time Singularities of the $L_\beta$-Gradient Flow in a K\"ahler Surface
items.summary: We study finite-time singularities of the $L_\beta$-gradient flow of closed symplectic surfaces in a compact K\"ahler surface, with $\beta > 0$ fixed. We derive the evolution equation for the second fundamental form and obtain a lower bound on the blow-up rate of its maximum squared norm. Combining this bound with a local curvature propagation estimate and the weighted monotonicity formula, we rule out Type I singularities.

Transforming their image-order intensities into signed Fourier visibilities reveals separate critical-curve oscillations and a narrow-ring modulation scale in the unresolved sum. items.title: Enumerative Chromatic Choosability of Complete Multipartite Graphs with Small Partite Sets
items.summary: Chromatic choosability is a notion of fundamental importance in list coloring. A graph is chromatic-choosable when its chromatic number is equal to its list chromatic number. In their 1979 paper on list coloring, Erd\H{o}s, Rubin, and Taylor showed that complete $m$-partite graphs with every partite set of size 2, denoted by $K_{2*m}$, are chromatic-choosable. In 1990, Kostochka and Sidorenko introduced the list color function of a graph $G$, denoted by $P_{\ell}(G,m)$, which is the list analogue of the chromatic polynomial of $G$, $P(G,m)$. A graph $G$ is enumeratively chromatic-choosable when $P_{\ell}(G,m) = P(G,m)$ whenever $m \in \mathbb{N}$. In this paper, we explore the question as…

items.title: Numerical Integration of Geodesic Motion in Non-Schwarzschild Spacetimes
items.summary: This contribution presents a method for numerically solving geodesic motion in Wolfram Mathematica applied on a system consisting of a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a thin Vogt-Letelier disk. While geodesic motion in the Schwarzschild spacetime is fully integrable due to its high degree of symmetry, the addition of a disk breaks the spherical symmetry and leads to a weak-integrable dynamical system. Particular attention is paid to the treatment of particle trajectories near the thin disk, where discontinuities in the derivatives of the metric may affect numerical stability and the conservation of integrals of motion. Several numerical treatments of disk crossings were implemented…

items.title: Blow-up phenomena and ill-posedness for the 2D Euler-Poincar\'e equations
items.summary: In this paper, we study finite-time blow-up and critical norm inflation for the Euler--Poincar\'e equations on $\mathbb R^2$. We consider a class of momentum fields admitting the div--curl decomposition with radial scalar potentials. The potentials satisfy a nonlocal transport system. By virtue of the conservation law and the finite propagation speed property, we obtain a growth estimate for the potential, which yields a sufficient condition for finite-time blow-up. Furthermore, combining a multiscale construction of the initial data with a blow-up criterion formulated in terms of the Besov norm of the deformation tensor, we establish norm inflation at the zero initial datum in…

items.title: Gravitomagnetic Frame Memory
items.summary: We investigate the response of spatially separated spinning test particles to a finite-duration plane gravitational wave in the proper detector frame, {working to linear order in the wave amplitude.} Using Fermi normal coordinates and the gravitoelectromagnetic decomposition of the local metric, the spin evolution is governed, at leading order in the distance from the reference world-line, by the magnetic part of the Riemann tensor. A finite curvature profile with a non-vanishing gravitomagnetic pulse area induces a residual relative rotation of the spins, proportional to the time integral of the local gravitomagnetic field. The resulting change persists after the curvature has vanished…

items.title: Extragalactic carbon-monoxide (CO) as a CMB foreground: an analytic halo model for the CO auto-spectrum and its correlation with the Cosmic Infrared Background
items.summary: Context. Carbon Monoxide (CO) lines emitted by star-forming galaxies are redshifted into the frequency bands of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) experiments. Their correlation with the Cosmic Infrared Background (CIB) may be a non-negligible small-scale foreground. Aims. We develop an analytic, full-shape halo model framework for the CO auto-spectrum and for the CO$\times$CIB cross-spectrum in CMB bands, and assess its impact on current and future high-resolution CMB experiments. Methods. We use a luminosity-weighted halo model with separate occupation distributions of central and satellite galaxies for CO and CIB emitters, CO transitions up to $J=13$, and all auto- and…

items.title: Exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon field in planar systems with an arbitrary number of uniform layers
items.summary: Scalar fields have long been investigated as a potential dark energy candidate. Of these models, screened scalar fields like the chameleon have received interest due to their ability to avoid observational constraints. However, the non-linear nature of these models has led to there being only a small number of exact analytic solutions within the literature. In this work, we present exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon model in a planar system consisting of $N$ discrete regions of uniform density. We compare these to the relevant approximate solutions within the literature. We also use our solutions to forecast constraints from CANNEX, a recent experiment devised to measure…

items.title: A Characterization of Tangle Matroids
items.summary: We prove that a matroid with at least two elements is a tangle matroid if and only if it cannot be covered by three hyperplanes. Some consequences of this theorem are also noted. In particular, no binary matroid of rank at least two is a tangle matroid.

items.title: A Constructive Lower Bound for the Growth Constant of Ternary Cap Sets
items.summary: Let $r_3(d)$ denote the maximum size of a cap set in $\mathbb{F}_3^d$. We prove that the exponential growth constant $\Lambda = \lim_{d\to\infty} r_3(d)^{1/d}$ is strictly greater than $2.22920646813$. The main advance comes from combining two-color recursive synchronization with cross-layer joint filling of a seven-dimensional local alphabet that contains collinear triples (lines). By encoding marked positions as $14$-step closed walks on a two-state directed graph, any zero-sum triple with a fixed outermost color is forced to choose the identical closed walk---and hence the identical record---at every recursive layer, at a net cost of $1000$ dimensions per level. Because the open…

items.title: SchemaCaps: When a Compatible Tool Update Silently Widens an AI Agent's Authority
items.summary: The tools users approve for their AI agents keep changing their JSON input schemas. Of 8 surveyed MCP clients and scanners, none is observed or documented to re-approve a tool whose input schema widens (two not determinable). We define non-amplification over the coordinates visible in the schema (declared arguments and undeclared fields, on effective values) and a re-binding rule decided by subschema inclusion, trusting no field labels by default and conservative up to its checker and tested case analysis. Evidence: a Coq proof of composition; 48 regression tests; an exact-reference benchmark, where the reviewed version of the rule silently re-bound 27 amplifying changes, now fixed; and a…

items.title: WIMPs as FIMPs: the Inert Doublet Model and low-temperature reheating
items.summary: Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) are conventionally assumed to acquire their dark matter relic abundance through thermal freeze-out. However, this association relies on assumptions concerning the thermal history of the early Universe. We revisit the Inert Doublet Model (IDM), a representative WIMP framework in which dark matter interacts with the Standard Model through electroweak gauge interactions, even when its Higgs-portal coupling vanishes. We demonstrate that sufficiently low reheating temperatures can prevent chemical equilibrium, allowing a genuine WIMP to acquire its relic abundance through freeze-in rather than freeze-out. Considering both instantaneous and…

items.title: Reverse Schensted bumping, inverse reduction map and concatenation in the inverse quantum Littlewood-Richardson bijection
items.summary: Provided the explicit formula for the inverse reduction map, arXiv:2606.24840, we exhibit for symplectic bumped intervals and for symplectic bumped columns disjoint for the action of the parity involution, the feasibility of the concatenation operation to return a semi-standard tableau in the inverse quantum Littlewood-Richardson bijection

items.title: Persistence and Breakdown of the Initial Gaussian Rate Function for 1D Quasi-Periodic Cubic NLS
items.summary: We study rare events for the spatial supremum of the solution amplitude in the 1D cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with weak nonlinearity and Gaussian quasi-periodic initial data.Under suitable polynomial decay assumptions in Fourier space and a Diophantine condition controlling small divisors arising from spatial quasi-periodicity, we prove that the initial Gaussian rate function persists uniformly on the \emph{critical logarithmic correction time scale} with a \emph{small enough} prefactor. Using the \emph{Akhmediev breather}, we obtain that the same Gaussian rate function \emph{fails} to hold uniformly on this time scale with a \emph{large} prefactor. This also implies that the…

items.title: The Sensitivity of Gamma-Ray Searches for Dark Matter Annihilation in Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies: the LSST Era and Beyond
items.summary: We forecast the sensitivity of gamma-ray searches to dark matter annihilation in Milky Way satellite dwarf galaxies using BabyBison, a Monte Carlo pipeline combining cosmological satellite simulations and observational selection functions with a joint likelihood analysis of gamma-ray data. Although LSST is expected to substantially expand the catalog of known satellite galaxies, we find that these discoveries are likely to produce only modest improvements in the resulting dark matter annihilation constraints, typically below 20\%. Much more substantial gains are possible, however, in relatively rare realizations that contain yet-to-be-discovered satellites with large $J$-factors. These…

items.title: Sharp Estimates for Jacobi Heat Kernels on a Ball and on a Simplex in the Full Range of Parameters
items.summary: We establish genuinely sharp heat-kernel estimates for orthogonal expansions on the Euclidean unit ball and on the unit simplex throughout their natural parameter ranges. For the ball weight $W_\mu(x)=(1-\|x\|^2)^{\mu-1/2}$, we extend the known estimate from the range $\mu\geq0$ to every $\mu>-1/2$. For the simplex, we prove the corresponding estimate for every $\kappa\in(-1/2,\infty)^{d+1}$. The estimates retain exactly the form known in the classical ranges. The proof is based on analytic continuation of the classical product and reduction formulas. Below the integrability threshold, the ball formula decomposes into an endpoint term and a derivative correction, while the simplex formula…

items.title: An Intergalactic medium centred parametrisation of the 21-cm power spectrum from the Epoch of Reionization
items.summary: The 21-cm signal from the intergalactic medium (IGM) is a key probe of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR). In this work, we present a model of the 21-cm power spectrum centred on the state of the IGM. The framework combines aspects of perturbation and percolation theory to deduce a physically informed parametrisation of the power spectrum. Moreover, it complements classical interpretation methods, centred on modelling the properties of the first ionising sources. We define the IGM parameters driving the shape and amplitude of the 21-cm signal, from the globally averaged volume- and mass-weighted ionisation fractions ($\bar{x}_{HII}$ and $\bar{x}_{HIIm}$), the clustering of sources, through…

items.title: Path Integrals on Functional Lattices
items.summary: Path integrals in quantum field theory are commonly approached through finite-dimensional approximations, but existence and regulator independence of the infinite-dimensional limit require separate analysis. We introduce a scheme in which spacetime remains continuous and the field is expanded in a discrete complete family of localized functions, called a functional lattice. Truncation to finite-dimensional functional subspaces yields ordinary finite-dimensional integrals while leaving the continuum differential operator unchanged. For the massive free Euclidean scalar field, we prove convergence of the finite-dimensional covariance operators and normalized generating functionals by a…

items.title: Nonabelianization map for the $W_{3,c=2}$ conformal blocks. Part I
items.summary: This work is inspired by the nonabelianization construction of Virasoro conformal blocks. We start the process of defining the nonabelianization map which expresses $c=2$ $W_3$-algebra conformal blocks on a Riemann surface $C$ from Heisenberg blocks on a branched triple cover $\tilde{C}$ of $C$. This generalized nonabelianization map uses the datum of a $\mathfrak{gl}_3$ spectral network on $C$ and we find that this map also depends on the soliton degeneracies corresponding to the spectral network even though the soliton data didn't show up explicitly in the Virasoro case. This nonabelianization construction defines new formulas for $W_3$-algebra conformal blocks on $C$ in terms of fermion…

items.title: Shifted moments of angular Hecke $L$-functions
items.summary: In this paper, we establish upper bounds for shifted moments of angular Hecke $L$-function over imaginary quadratic number fields of class number one under the generalized Riemann hypothesis. The result is used to derive bounds for moments of angular Hecke character sums.

items.title: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals: accessing generic orbits
items.summary: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRI) are a significant gravitational wave source and a target for the upcoming LISA mission. Computations of the fluxes of conserved quantities, such as energy and angular momentum, are a critical part of modeling EMRI waveforms and can be performed using a frequency domain formalism to solve the Teukolsky equation. This requires computations of large numbers of mode amplitudes, many of which are negligible. However, it is unknown ex ante which can be safely skipped. We present a machine learning approach to estimate the dominant radial mode number as a function of the remaining mode numbers and apply it to reduce the number of unnecessary computations in…

items.title: Short Paper No. 2: Relations between integer sequences A003622 $\&$ A035336 and two criteria in respect of maximum degrees within the family of finite linear Jaco graphs
items.summary: This paper establishes two relationships between integer sequences and the maximum degrees of finite linear Jaco graphs $J_n(x)$. First, it characterizes the positive maximum degrees that occur exactly once within the family, showing that they are generated by the integer sequence A003622. Second, it determines the orders of the corresponding graphs and establishes their relationship with the integer sequence A035336. These results resolve conjectures previously stated in [5]. The proofs were developed with the assistance of AI-based mathematical reasoning technology and subsequently reviewed by the authors.

items.title: Resolution of ladder representations for classical groups
items.summary: Atobe has introduced ladder representations of the $p$-adic groups $\mathbf{Sp}(2n)$ and $\mathbf{SO}(2n+1)$, which contain the strongly positive discrete series and M\oe glin's representations attached to irreducible Arthur parameters, and has expressed their characters as alternating sums of costandard modules. We show that all the coefficients of this formula are $\pm1$, with the sign given by the dimension of the orbit of the Langlands parameter, and that these representations have coresolutions of Cousin type by costandard modules, whose Euler characteristic is Atobe's formula.

items.title: The dimension of optimal plans in multi-marginal optimal transport
items.summary: For general cost functions, we determine the maximal dimension on which solutions to the multi-marginal optimal transport problem with absolutely continuous marginals are concentrated. The dimension is obtained via a novel characteristic integer associated with the Hessian of the cost function. Applications are given to important examples of multi-marginal problems like Wasserstein barycenters, Wasserstein cubic splines and Brenier's generalized Euler equations.

items.title: Quantitative thick-fiber property
items.summary: We introduce the quantitative thick-fiber property, an analogue of the Entov--Polterovich non-displaceable fiber theorem for maps whose coordinate functions need not Poisson commute. We prove that this property holds for closed symplectic manifolds admitting a suitable, not necessarily linear, functional on the space of continuous functions. Conversely, we establish an obstruction and show that the property fails for certain irrational symplectic four-tori and Kodaira--Thurston manifolds. These results reveal a new rigidity--flexibility distinction: whereas the Entov--Polterovich theorem gives a universal fiber-rigidity phenomenon, its quantitative counterpart holds on some closed…

items.title: Support monotonicity for quadratically regularized optimal transport
items.summary: We study the support of the optimizer $\pi_\varepsilon$ of the quadratically regularized optimal transport problem for quadratic cost and compactly supported marginals. As $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, this support converges to the support of the Monge coupling. We investigate whether the regularized supports are nested as $\varepsilon $ decreases. Under regularity assumptions on the marginal densities, their domains, and the Brenier map, we establish interior support inclusions in every dimension. More precisely, for each compact $K\subset\operatorname{int}X$ and fixed $\theta\in(0,1)$, we prove that $\mathrm{spt}\pi_\delta\cap(K\times Y) \subseteq\mathrm{spt}\pi_\varepsilon\cap(K\times…

items.title: $K3$ Picard--Fuchs equations with initial conditions in the Hodge line
items.summary: Lam and Litt conjectured that a formal horizontal section of a Gauss--Manin connection is algebraic if and only if it is integral, if and only if it is $\omega(p)$-integral. We prove it for families of $K3$ surfaces over a finitely generated $\mathbb Z$-algebra in a number field, when the initial condition lies in the Hodge line. In this case, all three conditions are equivalent to the vanishing of the Higgs field on the Hodge line. Along the way, we show that a smooth projective family $X\to S$ with $H^0(X_s,T_{X_s})=0$ is constant on an \'{e}tale neighborhood of $s$ if and only if its Kodaira--Spencer class vanishes near $s$.

items.title: Symplectizing stable generalized complex four-manifolds
items.summary: We explicitly describe a surgery that turns a stable generalized complex four-manifold into a symplectic four-manifold. As a consequence, we show that for $n\geq 2$, the almost complex manifold $(n^2+n+1)S^1\times S^3\#\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$ admits no stable generalized complex structures or constant type generalized complex structures. We also prove an irreducibility result for stable generalized complex four-manifolds and we show that the moduli space of generalized complex structures on an elliptic surface has infinitely many components.

items.title: Constraining Dehnen-inspired dark matter halo with S2 star's orbit
items.summary: We use the orbit of S2 star around Sagittarius A* to constrain three black hole backgrounds motivated by Dehnen profiles with inner slopes $\gamma=0$, $1$, and $5/2$, which are characterized by the scale radius $r_s$ and density $\rho_s$ of the dark matter halo. An exact turning-point integral gives the pericenter advance at finite eccentricity, and an exterior expansion identifies the leading halo contributions. A fifteen-parameter Bayesian analysis combines astrometric and spectroscopic observations with the measured precession parameter, from which we obtain the marginalized $1\sigma$ upper limits $r_s/M<0.236$, $0.168$, and $0.030$, and $\rho_sM^2<0.536$, $0.578$, and $0.004$…

items.title: Combined quasi-neutral and zero-relaxation limit of Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system
items.summary: In this paper, we consider the combined quasi-neutral and zero-relaxation limit of Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system. With well-prepared initial, we show that the convergence from Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system for electron and Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system for ion to the incompressible Euler equations and compressible Euler equations, respectively.

items.title: Solvability of one-dimensional sub-quadratic BSDEs with unbounded stochastic coefficients
items.summary: This study is devoted to solvability of the unbounded solutions of a class of one-dimensional sub-quadratic backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) with unbounded stochastic coefficients and general time horizons. In a general sub-exponential moment integrability space linked with the stochastic coefficients, we first establish existence of an unbounded solution of the preceding BSDE when the generator $g$ has a one-sided linear growth in the state variable $y$ and a sub-quadratic growth in the state variable $z$, and then prove a comparison theorem of the unbounded solutions of such two BSDEs when either of generators satisfies an extended convexity/concavity condition in…

items.title: The Simons Observatory: Analysis of methods for polarization calibration of multiple instruments
items.summary: Cosmic birefringence, the rotation of the CMB linear polarization plane across the Universe, is a powerful test of parity-violating physics beyond the Standard Model. Static isotropic rotation, however, is limited by an instrument's absolute polarization-angle calibration. We present a method for transferring absolute calibration between Simons Observatory (SO) instruments, validated on map-level simulations of the Large Aperture Telescope (LAT) and Small Aperture Telescopes (SATs) with lensed CMB polarization, polarized Galactic foregrounds, correlated instrumental noise, and polarization-angle miscalibration. We develop two pipelines: a joint LAT+SAT likelihood transferring calibration…

items.title: Thermodynamics of hard wall model of AdS/QCD at finite chemical potential with Gauss-Bonnet corrections
items.summary: We study the confinement/deconfinement transition of the hard wall model of AdS/QCD at finite quark density in five-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell--Gauss--Bonnet gravity, with the back-reaction of the quark matter on the geometry included. The deconfined phase is a charged Gauss--Bonnet black hole, and the confined phase is thermally charged AdS cut off in the infrared. The infrared value of the gauge field, which Lee, Park and Sin fixed by requiring a consistent quark number, becomes a function of the Gauss--Bonnet coupling. We obtain the transition line in closed form at fixed quark chemical potential and at fixed quark number density. At fixed density the transition passes through a…

items.title: Early Evolution of Strange Quark Stars Admixed with Fermionic Dark Matter
items.summary: We study strange quark stars admixed with fermionic dark matter (DM) in three quasistatic stages of their early evolution: the neutrino-trapped stage, the heated stage after deleptonization, and the cold stage. Quark matter is described by the MIT bag model at finite temperature with thermal gluons, a repulsive vector interaction, and, in the first stage, trapped neutrinos. The DM is modeled as a cold, asymmetric gas of fermions with masses $m_\chi = 0.3$, $1$, and $3$ GeV, with and without a repulsive self-interaction, and interacts with the quark matter only through gravity. Using the two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, we compute the structure, the maximum masses, and the…

items.title: Essential and disjoint edge numbers for graphs and hypergraphs
items.summary: We study the extension to arbitrary forbidden sets of the property that every graph has a bipartition over which at least half of the graph edges are cross-edges, and obtain analogous results in the hypergraph setting.

items.title: Relativistic dynamical friction and accretion for Kerr black holes
items.summary: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) observed by LISA will probe the environments of massive black holes (BHs), including the dark matter (DM) overdensities expected to form around them. We compute the relativistic dynamical friction and accretion experienced by a non-spinning compact object on circular equatorial orbits around a Kerr BH embedded in a collisionless DM distribution, extending previous results in Schwarzschild. The DM is modeled as a spike grown adiabatically from an initial Hernquist profile, and the momentum transfer is obtained by integrating relativistic scattering and capture cross sections over the full, generically anisotropic phase space seen by the secondary. Far…

items.title: FMSNO: Scaling Surface Neural Operators by Learned Flow Matching Reparametrisation
items.summary: We propose the Flow Matching Surface Neural Operator (FMSNO), which combines learning a shared map from irregular surface meshes to a regular two-dimensional grid on the sphere and training a neural operator on the regular grid. Constructing a separate map for each new geometry can dominate inference time on large meshes. We initially pretrain the mapping by flow matching using precomputed optimal transport maps as targets and then continue its training using combined geometry and CFD objectives. We apply it to unseen geometries in a single forward pass. The learned flow deforms the surface points, and we project its endpoints onto the sphere. We then splat geometric features onto the…

items.title: Notes on an elementary proof of Weil II from Hexagon
items.summary: Recently, L. Alp\"oge sketched an elementary proof of Deligne's weight bound in footnote 3 of his remark on joint work with Claude on the Riemann hypothesis. An expanded, AI-generated account appeared on Hexagon, where it was posted by F. Alderliefste. This note gives an exposition of the proof presented there.

items.title: Magic Production and the Fundamental Forces of Nature
items.summary: Quantum magic is a resource for universal quantum computation and may also provide a probe of fundamental interactions. We study its production in forward scattering of two distinct Standard Model fermions in the chirality basis. In the single-mediator-exchange approximation, magic production vanishes for gluon, photon, W-boson, Higgs-boson, and graviton exchange. For Z-boson exchange in purely leptonic scattering, it also vanishes at $\sin^2\theta_W = 1/4$, close to the phenomenological value. By contrast, Z-boson exchange involving elementary quarks generally produces nonzero magic. These patterns raise the question of whether the construction of the fundamental forces encodes, at least…

items.title: A generalization of L\'evy's stochastic area formula for Gaussian rough paths
items.summary: In this paper, we establish a generalization of L\'evy's stochastic area formula for the canonical rough path lift of a $2n$-dimensional centered Gaussian process with independent, identically distributed components. The formula extends the identity obtained by Aihara, Akahori, Fujii and Nitta [1] for Brownian motion. We compute the expectation of the exponential of a functional involving stochastic areas and quadratic forms in the terminal values. The result is expressed in terms of spectral data of a Hilbert--Schmidt operator associated with the stochastic area and an $n \times n$ determinant. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for absolute integrability in terms of the…

items.title: Global strong solvability of the two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes equations for large initial data
items.summary: In 1995, Kazhikhov and Vaigant introduced a two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes model with constant shear viscosity and bulk viscosity $\lambda(\rho)=\rho^\beta$. For $\beta>3$, they proved global existence of smooth solutions for arbitrarily large initial data with strictly positive density. More recently, Fan-Jiang-Li-L\"u (arXiv:2611.20264, 2026) proved global strong solvability for every $\beta>1$ in bounded simply connected domains with Navier-slip boundary conditions. In this article, we prove global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions to the Kazhikhov-Vaigant model on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ at the critical point $\beta=1$, for every $\gamma>1$ and…

items.title: Granular Mass Perturbations on the Pulsar-Supermassive Black Hole System
items.summary: Author(s): Zexin Hu and Lijing Shao The uncertain mass distribution of stars and compact objects in the galactic center significantly alter the timing uncertainty of the observed pulses from the pulsar orbiting the supermassive black hole at the center of our galaxy. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 211401] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026

items.title: Orbit-averaged spinning and eccentric binary black holes: Hamiltonian and integrability
items.summary: For over two decades, the orbit-averaged precession equations of spinning binary black holes at second post-Newtonian order have been a standard model for their spin dynamics. One of their constants of motion, the projected effective spin, underlies the stability analysis of aligned-spin configurations and the construction of analytical solutions. The system is known to be Hamiltonian and integrable, its Hamiltonian being the orbit average of the full post-Newtonian Hamiltonian. Independently, we derive this Hamiltonian from the equations of motion alone, show why the orbit average gives the correct equations, and relate its constants of motion to those of the full system. We then…

items.title: Search for Heavy Charged Higgs Bosons in Boosted Top and Bottom Quark Final States at a 1.4 TeV Future Lepton Collider
items.summary: The discovery potential for heavy charged Higgs bosons $H^\pm$ decaying into a top-bottom quark pair is investigated at a future $e^+e^-$ collider operating at $\sqrt{s}=1.4~\mathrm{TeV}$. The study considers charged Higgs masses between 200 and 600 GeV within all four Yukawa types of the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM). The boosted $tb$ final state is explored using complementary cut-based and machine-learning analyses based on boosted decision trees (BDT). The expected signal significance and sensitivity contours in the $(m_{H^\pm},\tan\beta)$ plane are obtained for each Yukawa type. The resulting sensitivity extends to regions of the 2HDM parameter space beyond the projected reach of the…

items.title: An $\infty$-category approach to $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories
items.summary: $A_\infty$-algebras over a commutative ring $R$ are generalizations of $R$-algebras in which multiplication is only associative up to higher homotopies. Similarly, $A_\infty$-categories over $R$ are generalizations of $R$-linear categories in which composition of morphisms is only associative up to higher homotopies. They are important in the definition of Fukaya categories in Symplectic Geometry, and in other areas of mathematics. By $\infty$-categories we mean quasicategories, a class of simplicial sets which are a model for $(\infty,1)$-categories, used in the work of Jacob Lurie. We define and study $\infty$-categories of $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories. Our approach is…

items.title: Root-of-Unity Limits of Trigonometric qKZ Connections
items.summary: Over the field of complex numbers, we study root-of-unity limits of trigonometric qKZ connections associated with tensor products of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ Verma modules and of their hypergeometric solutions. As the multiplicative step approaches a primitive $m$-th root of unity and the quantum-group and twist parameters approach $1$, the $m$-step qKZ transport yields, on every fixed-degree subspace,a differential connection. We show that this connection is the pullback of the trigonometric KZ connection under the power map $z\mapsto z^m$, with the KZ parameter rescaled by $m$, and establish formal and $\ell$-adic versions. In degree one, with all highest weights equal to $1$, we determine…

items.title: Testing the Universality of RAR Model with Constraints on Fermionic Dark Matter for M31
items.summary: The Ruffini--Arg\"uelles--Rueda (RAR) model describes dark matter as a self-gravitating system of massive fermions in thermodynamic equilibrium within general relativity. It suggests a dual morphology in galaxies: a highly degenerate quantum core mimicking a central supermassive black hole, and a classical halo that explains galactic rotation curves. Earlier applications of the model to the Milky Way restricted the fermion mass to $mc^{2}=48\text{--}345~\text{keV}$, and the orbits of the S-stars around Sagittarius~A$^{\ast}$ (Sgr~A$^{\ast}$) favored $mc^{2}=56~\text{keV}$, whereas a recent thermodynamic stability analysis allows only $mc^{2}\approx194\text{--}387~\text{keV}$. items.title: Soft Factorisation of WQFT and the Spinning 4PM Magnusian
items.summary: We derive the soft divergences of $\hat{N}=-i\log\hat{S}$ in the Worldline Quantum Field Theory (WQFT) formalism, focusing on poles due to single massive-massive (Coulomb) and massive-massless (tail) graviton exchanges. Our derivation is inspired by the Faddeev-Kulish procedure, switching the interaction picture to one with an infrared-finite $\hat{N}$-matrix. Soft divergences emerging from the worldline are correlators of Wilson lines. items.title: Thermal Resummation Effects on Electroweak Phase Transitions and Gravitational Waves in Conformal and Non-Conformal 2HDMs
items.summary: We quantify how thermal resummation affects electroweak phase transitions and gravitational-wave predictions in classically conformal and non-conformal two-Higgs-doublet models. We compare multi-field partial dressing (PD), which retains the full thermal functions and determines scalar masses and mixing from gap equations, with the Parwani and Arnold-Espinosa (AE) prescriptions at identical zero-temperature inputs. Completed first-order transitions dominate the conformal scan under all three prescriptions. PD typically gives the strongest and most supercooled transitions, reaching $T_p/T_c \simeq 0.5$ versus $T_p/T_c \gtrsim 0.8$ for Parwani and AE. At every conformal point where all three…

items.title: Quiver-Invariant Triality between Brane Brick Models
items.summary: We study quiver-invariant triality between 2d (0,2) supersymmetric gauge theories described by brane brick models associated with toric Calabi-Yau 4-folds. The dual theories share the same gauge groups, field content and E-terms but have distinct J-terms. We present an explicit pair of such brane brick models and identify the sequence of triality mutations relating them. This sequence returns the quiver to its original form while transforming the J- and E-terms. We explain the relation between quiver-invariant triality and the orbifold reduction of quiver-invariant brane tilings.

items.title: The BSM Rollercoaster, 1980-2000
items.summary: This contribution is a personal historical retrospective on beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) physics from 1978 to the early 2000s, organized around its emotional rollercoaster. I trace two waves of optimism separated by a multiyear contraction of confidence, both ultimately ending in disappointment when decisive experimental confirmation failed to arrive. The story begins in 1978, when the Standard Model emerged as the front-runner. It then moves from the first wave of excitement over naturalness and Technicolor, rumored proton-decay events, and the construction of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, to the contraction of confidence in the late 1980s. A dramatic revival came in 1991…

items.title: Scherk-Schwarz Compactifications: From Circles to Strings
items.summary: This review is written with a simple question in mind: what does one need to know to enter the literature on Scherk-Schwarz compactifications? It is organized as a sequence of questions that a graduate student might naturally ask, together with the concepts, calculations, and formal tools needed to work through the literature. The discussion starts at an elementary field-theory level and gradually develops toward more advanced aspects of supergravity, orbifolds, quantum effects, and string theory. Phenomenological applications are deliberately left aside.

items.title: Accretion disks and photon rings in Palatini Kalb-Ramond gravity
items.summary: We investigate thin accretion disks and photon rings around a static black hole in Palatini Kalb Ramond gravity, connecting thermal emission with the optical effects of the radial geometry. At fixed orbital mass and accretion rate, the local radiative flux scales as $1/\sigma$ and the effective temperature as $1/\sigma^{1/4}$, where $\sigma=\sqrt{1-q/2}$ and $q$ is the effective curvature coupling. The innermost stable circular orbit and the critical impact parameter share their Schwarzschild values, together with an emitted efficiency of approximately $5.72\%$. Moreover, photon trajectories admit an exact angular rescaling that determines the strong deflection coefficient and the…

items.title: Cardinal RG=GR: Phase-Space Cardinality and the Cosmological Constant and Hierarchy Problems
items.summary: The effective field theory approach constructs the low-energy theory by integrating out fluctuations above an ultraviolet scale which raises the cosmological constant and hierarchy problems. We investigate an alternative prescription in which the quantum theory is restricted to a finite accessible region of phase space, characterized by a dimensionless cardinality $\mathcal N$, rather than by independently prescribed spacetime and momentum scales. At fixed cardinality these scales are related. For Euclidean de Sitter space, the stationarity condition for the gravitational action can then be written as a stationarity condition with respect to the momentum scale, a relation which we call…

items.title: UV Bounds on Inflationary Parity Violation
items.summary: A question of fundamental interest is whether parity is violated on large scales in the Universe. This possibility has been motivated by recent analyses of the four-point matter correlation function. It has also been suggested that detectable parity violation could be generated during inflation by the dynamical Chern-Simons operator, a leading effective field theory correction to general relativity. In this work, we examine this possibility in realistic UV completions, including fermionic and string-theoretic examples. We show that existing bounds on the tensor-scalar-scalar (TSS) bispectrum strongly constrain the possibility of generating a detectable parity-odd trispectrum. For…

items.title: A Hopf algebra action on the cohomology of moduli of abelian varieties
items.summary: We show that the rational compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal{A} = \bigsqcup_{g \geq 0} \mathcal{A}_g$ of principally polarized abelian varieties is free as a bigraded module over the Hopf algebra formed by its weight-zero subspace. The action arises from a symplectic analog of the Waldhausen $S$-construction. This structure yields new lower bounds for Betti numbers and the dimensions of the graded pieces of the weight filtration on the cohomology of $\mathcal{A}_g$. In particular, $\dim H_c^{2g + k}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ grows at least exponentially with $g$ for every nonnegative $k \neq 1, 3$. We also give conjectural descriptions of the full mixed Hodge structures in…

items.title: A Tensor-Algebraic No-Go Theorem for High-Dimensional Photonic Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger States Discovered with AlphaProof Nexus
items.summary: Photonic GHZ states generated with probabilistic pair sources can be described by edge-coloured, complex-weighted graphs. In this representation, conditioning on an event with one photon in every detector turns the output amplitudes into coherent sums over perfect matchings, and generating an \(N\)-photon \(D\)-dimensional GHZ state is equivalent to constructing a monochromatic quantum graph. Here, we prove that no complex-weighted monochromatic quantum graph exists for any even \(N\ge4\) when \(D\ge N\). The proof, discovered through AI-assisted formal proof search in Lean using AlphaProof Nexus, constructs a weighted sum \(\mathcal F\) of amplitudes whose coefficients factor vertex by…

items.title: Exact ultrastatic multi-throat wormholes: Geometry, energy conditions, and optical cavities
items.summary: We construct an exactly solvable hierarchy of static, spherically symmetric, wormholes with arbitrary finite throat multiplicity. A factorized prescription for the derivative of the areal radius places every stationary sphere at a prescribed proper distance while retaining elementary integrability and asymptotic flatness. The order-$N$ geometry contains exactly $N+1$ throats and $N$ anti-throats, arranged as an alternating chain of necks and finite interior cavities. Independently of this particular hierarchy, the Einstein equations imply three universal ultrastatic results. Every nondegenerate throat violates the radial null energy condition, whereas every nondegenerate anti-throat…

items.title: Entanglement entropy from fundamental strings
items.summary: In previous work, we derived the local entropy capacity from off-shell string theory and combined it with the gravitational replica construction and flow-cut duality to normalize the entropy flow carried by physical fundamental strings. In this paper, we apply this framework to interval entanglement in holographic CFT$_2$. We construct explicit on-shell F1 worldsheets in the AdS$_3$ vacuum and planar BTZ, derive their Kalb-Ramond source currents, and show that the normalized spatial currents saturate the corresponding RT surface. Their flux reproduces both the vacuum single interval entropy and the finite temperature CFT$_2$ result. We then vary the NS-NS flux fraction. Although the total…

items.title: Supersymmetric Hilbert complexes and Witten deformation on stratified pseudomanifolds
items.summary: We present a framework to study topics related to index theory and Dirac operators with N=1,2 supersymmetry (SUSY), extending it to stratified pseudomanifolds with wedge metrics (iterated conic metrics). We use this to construct Witten deformed subcomplexes of SUSY Hilbert complexes that categorify Morse polynomials and equivariant index formulae for a large class of operators. This allows us to prove equivariant index theorems for spin-c Dirac operators with Hamiltonian actions, and Holomorphic Morse inequalities in the K\"ahler case, in particular proving a new type of equivariant Riemann-Roch (ERR) theorem on singular spaces. We also improve on stratified Morse-Bott inequalities in the…

items.title: Actionless Branes on Axion Wormholes
items.summary: Can a Euclidean axion wormhole extend to infinity with every instanton still suppressed? The imaginary distance bound says it cannot: some instanton must become actionless first. Calabi-Yau compactifications appear to violate the bound: several axions share the field excursion, and the instantons charged under any one of them stay suppressed all the way. We show that the wormhole can hide from these instantons but not from their bound states: misaligned central charges make a bound state cheaper than its constituents, while the axions act on every constituent. On the type IIB wormhole supported by two axions of the Neveu-Schwarz two-form, a fivebrane carrying string charge becomes…

items.title: Algebraic matroids with non-algebraic duals exist in any positive characteristic
items.summary: We show that for every field $K$ of positive characteristic there exists an algebraic matroid $M$ over $K$ such that the dual matroid $M^*$ is not algebraic over any field. Our conceptual proof relies on the theory of matroids over one-dimensional algebraic groups. As an application, we deduce that the classes of supports of realizable volume polynomials and of realizable covolume polynomials differ in positive characteristic.

items.title: Review of Pion and Nucleon Gluon Parton Distribution Functions from Lattice QCD
items.summary: Gluons play an essential role in the strong interaction that binds quarks into hadrons, as described by quantum chromodynamics (QCD). Understanding how the fundamental dynamics of QCD give rise to hadron structure remains one of the outstanding challenges in nuclear and particle physics. Parton distribution functions (PDFs) provide a successful framework for describing high-energy scattering processes involving hadrons. However, our knowledge of gluon PDFs remains comparatively limited because of the experimental challenges associated with directly constraining the gluon structure of hadrons. In recent years, a major breakthrough has enabled the calculation of the Bjorken-$x$ dependence of…

items.summary: Extending the arithmetic Selberg-zeta function framework studied by Sarnak \cite{Sarnak1982} and Hashimoto \cite{Hashimoto2007}, we study Dirichlet-character weighted sums of narrow class numbers of real quadratic orders and derive explicit formulas according to the scalar, split, ramified, and inert reductions of primitive hyperbolic classes. Our first main result establishes asymptotic formulas for the class number sums associated with the three noninert reduction types and shows that, after multiplication by the corresponding nontrivial even-character weights, their leading terms cancel exactly for every fixed prime $p\ge 5$. Computational experiments across the sampled ranges of levels…

items.title: Degree Lower Bounds for Symmetric Boolean Functions: Breaking the Prime-Gap Barrier
items.summary: We prove that every nonconstant symmetric Boolean function on $n$ variables has exact real polynomial degree at least $n-O(n^{1/3}(\log n)^{2/3})$. This makes progress toward the conjecture of von zur Gathen and Roche that the degree is always at least $n-3$. The original prime-gap argument of von zur Gathen and Roche yields a degree deficit of $O(n^{0.525})$ using the theorem of Baker, Harman, and Pintz, or $O(n^{0.52})$ using an estimate claimed in a recent preprint. Our $\widetilde{O}(n^{1/3})$ bound on the degree deficit improves upon the $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{n})$ bound obtainable from the prime-gap approach, even assuming the Riemann hypothesis or Legendre's conjecture. items.title: Transferring an analysis of human brain organization to language models
items.summary: During human cortical development, functional systems become increasingly differentiated. We asked whether improved reasoning in language models involves a comparable regional reorganization. Applying diffusion-map embedding, used to characterize cortical organization, to matched base and reasoning-trained models from three families, we found broadly preserved gradient profiles with localized changes within a contiguous layer span. Grafting weights from these spans into instruction-tuned hosts improved mathematical reasoning on average, with gains rising with region overlap, while retaining more previously solved problems than grafts elsewhere. Across training, the span formed gradually…
